mergedParams.userDescription: A clean, smooth 'pop' scale-up, like a UI notification. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Smooth Pop-Up Text Animation for UI Notifications

prompts.prompt: Create a clean 'pop' typography preset that mimics the subtle bounce and scale animation of mobile notification bubbles. Each word or phrase should appear with a smooth scale-up from 85% to 100% size, with a subtle overshoot to 102% before settling back to 100% - like the elastic animation when iOS notifications appear. The text should start completely invisible (opacity 0) and fade in during the first 20% of the scale animation for a soft entrance. Position text elements centrally by default with optional staggering for multi-word sequences. Think of it as editing a title sequence where each word 'pops' into frame with perfect timing - not too aggressive, but with just enough energy to catch attention. The animation should feel organic and friendly, like the satisfying feedback you get from well-designed UI interactions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex items-center justify-center w-full h-full' for centered composition. Implement TextAtom components with generic keyframe effects using spring easing. Create an effect array with opacity animating from 0 to 1 over the first 0.2 of the range, and scale animating from 0.85 to 1.02 then settling to 1.0 using three keyframes at 0%, 70%, and 100% of the animation range. For caption-based typography, iterate through words array and apply staggered start times with 0.1-0.15 second delays between words. Use relative timing with each word's animation lasting 0.5-0.6 seconds. Consider adding a subtle blur effect from 2px to 0px during the scale-up for depth. Implement as a typography preset that accepts caption data and creates individual TextAtom components for each word with their own effect ranges based on word timing metadata.

prompts.prompt: Design a sophisticated 'notification pop' preset that treats text like UI toast notifications sliding up from the bottom while scaling. Imagine editing a modern app promo video where feature callouts appear as floating notification cards. The text should slide upward (translateY from 20px to 0) while simultaneously scaling from 0 to 100% with a smooth ease-out curve. Add a subtle shadow that grows during the animation to create the illusion of the text lifting off the surface. The preset should support both single words and full sentences, with sentence-level animations for headlines and word-level for body text. Consider this as creating motion graphics for a tech product launch - clean, professional, but with personality.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' as container. For notification-style layout, use 'absolute bottom-0 left-1/2 transform -translate-x-1/2' positioning. Apply compound effects: translateY from 20 to 0, scale from 0 to 1, and opacity from 0 to 1, all with ease-out easing over 0.4 seconds. Add dynamic shadow using filter or textShadow property animating from '0 0 0 transparent' to '0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)'. For typography presets, check caption data impact scores - high impact words get 10% larger scale and 0.1s longer duration. Create an internal effect preset called 'notification-pop' that combines these animations for reusability. Support both word-level and sentence-level modes via input parameter.

prompts.prompt: Build a minimalist 'pulse-pop' kinetic typography preset inspired by Apple Keynote animations. Text should materialize with a gentle pulsing scale effect - starting from a tiny point (5% scale), rapidly expanding to 110% scale, then easing back to 100% like a ripple settling. Layer this with a brightness pulse that makes the text briefly glow during the peak scale moment. This creates the feeling of text being 'activated' or 'powered on'. Perfect for title cards, chapter markers, or emphasis moments in video essays. The animation should read like a heartbeat on an editing timeline - quick expansion, gentle contraction, perfect stillness.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement with BaseLayout container using 'grid place-items-center min-h-screen' for perfect centering. Create TextAtom with multi-keyframe scale animation: 0% at 0.05, 40% at 1.1, 100% at 1.0 scale, using ease-in-out easing over 0.6 seconds total. Add brightness filter effect synchronized with scale: normal at start, 150% at peak scale, back to 100%. For enhanced visual interest, include a subtle rotate effect from -2deg to 0deg during scale-up. If using caption data, apply word-level timing with 0.08 second stagger between words. Consider creating a reusable 'pulse-pop' internal effect preset. For performance, use will-change: transform, filter on the TextAtom. Support customizable intensity via input parameter that scales all effect values proportionally.

prompts.prompt: Create an elegant 'bubble-float' typography animation that simulates text bubbling up like carbonation in a champagne glass. Each word should appear with a gentle wobble as it scales up, incorporating subtle horizontal sway (like bubbles don't rise perfectly straight). Start with text at 0% scale and opacity, then animate to 100% with a slight overshoot that includes random micro-movements. This evokes the feeling of effervescence and celebration - perfect for event titles, announcements, or playful captions. Think of it as editing celebratory moments where text needs to feel light, buoyant, and joyful.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex flex-col items-center justify-end h-full pb-12' to position text rising from bottom. Implement compound animation: scale from 0 to 1.05 to 1, translateY from 30px to -5px to 0, translateX with sine-wave oscillation between -3px and 3px. Apply spring easing for natural bounce physics. For word-level animations, add random variation to each word's translateX values (between -5px and 5px) to simulate natural bubble drift. Duration of 0.7-0.9 seconds per word with 0.12 second stagger. Include optional blur-to-focus effect (2px to 0) for depth. Create helper function to generate slight timing variations for organic feel. If keyword metadata is available in caption data, make important words 15% larger and rise slightly higher.

prompts.prompt: Develop a sharp, snappy 'digital glitch pop' preset that combines clean scaling with micro-glitch effects. Text scales from 0 to 100% but with 2-3 tiny 'digital hiccups' during the animation - brief moments where scale jumps to 95% or 105% for single frames, creating a controlled glitch aesthetic. Add subtle RGB color channel separation during these glitch moments. This style works brilliantly for tech content, gaming videos, or modern digital storytelling. Imagine cutting a cyberpunk title sequence where text materializes through digital interference before stabilizing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'relative isolate' for stacking context. Create primary TextAtom with scale animation including glitch keyframes: 0% at 0, 30% at 0.95, 32% at 1.05, 34% at 0.95, 70% at 1.03, 100% at 1.0. Use linear easing between glitch points for sharp transitions. Apply CSS filter for RGB split: 'drop-shadow(-2px 0 0 rgba(255,0,0,0.7)) drop-shadow(2px 0 0 rgba(0,255,255,0.7))' during glitch frames only. Total duration 0.5 seconds for punchy feel. For caption-based implementation, process words individually but synchronize glitch moments across all visible words for cohesive effect. Add optional 'intensity' parameter to control glitch frequency and amplitude. Consider using internal effect preset 'glitch-pop' for the complex keyframe sequence.

prompts.prompt: Design a smooth 'elastic bounce' kinetic type preset inspired by Material Design's motion principles. Text should stretch slightly on arrival - scaling to 100% width but 115% height momentarily, then bouncing back to perfect proportions. This creates a satisfying squash-and-stretch effect that feels physical and responsive. Layer in a subtle rotation wobble (-3deg to +3deg to 0) during the bounce for extra personality. Perfect for playful captions, call-to-action text, or anywhere you want text to feel touchable and interactive. Think of this as animating text that responds to user interaction in a video UI mockup.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement with BaseLayout container and TextAtom using scaleX and scaleY separately for squash-stretch effect. Keyframe sequence: Start at scaleX: 0, scaleY: 0; Peak at scaleX: 1.0, scaleY: 1.15; Settle to scaleX: 1.0, scaleY: 1.0. Add rotation: 0deg to -3deg to 3deg to 0deg over same timeline. Use cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for elastic easing. Duration of 0.6 seconds provides optimal bounce feel. For word-level typography, stagger by 0.1 seconds but keep all words' squash-stretch synchronized for cohesive motion. Include opacity fade from 0 to 1 over first 30% of animation. Apply 'transform-origin: center bottom' for grounded bounce effect. Support customizable elasticity parameter that adjusts overshoot percentages.

prompts.prompt: Create a refined 'focus pull' typography preset that mimics camera focus pulling techniques. Text starts extremely blurred (20px blur) and at 70% scale, then simultaneously scales to 100% while the blur reduces to 0, creating a cinematic 'coming into focus' effect. Add a subtle brightness boost during the focus transition to simulate the way focused subjects appear more vivid. This creates beautiful depth-of-field transitions perfect for documentary titles, photography portfolios, or cinematic text overlays. Imagine rack-focusing between text layers in a film title sequence.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full' and style transform3d for GPU acceleration. Apply compound effects to TextAtom: blur from 20px to 0px using filter property, scale from 0.7 to 1.0, opacity from 0.3 to 1.0, brightness from 80% to 110% to 100%. Use ease-in-out easing over 0.8 seconds for cinematic smoothness. For multi-word implementations, create depth layers by varying initial blur amounts (far words at 25px, near words at 15px) and staggering focus timing by 0.2 seconds. If using caption data, high-impact words should reach focus 0.1 seconds before others for emphasis. Include 'will-change: filter, transform' for performance. Consider adding subtle vignette overlay that fades out as text focuses for enhanced cinematic feel.

prompts.prompt: Develop a dynamic 'ripple reveal' preset where text appears to be dropped into water, creating concentric scaling ripples. The primary text scales from 0 to 100%, but ghost copies briefly appear at 120% and 140% scale with decreasing opacity, simulating ripple waves emanating outward. This creates a mesmerizing liquid effect perfect for wellness content, meditation apps, or any context requiring calm, flowing motion. Picture editing a spa commercial where text appears like droplets disturbing a still pool.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'relative grid place-items-center' as base. Create primary TextAtom with scale 0 to 1 over 0.5 seconds. Generate two additional TextAtom 'ripples' using repeatChildrenProps or cloning: First ripple scales 1.0 to 1.4 with opacity 0.5 to 0, starting 0.1 seconds after primary. Second ripple scales 1.0 to 1.8 with opacity 0.3 to 0, starting 0.2 seconds after primary. All use ease-out easing for natural ripple decay. Position ripples absolutely with 'absolute inset-0' and lower z-index. For caption-based implementation, each word creates its own ripple set with slight timing offsets (0.15 second stagger). Include optional 'rippleCount' and 'rippleSpread' parameters for customization. Consider using sub-preset for ripple generation to keep main preset clean.

prompts.prompt: Build an energetic 'spring-loaded' typography preset that feels like text is being launched from a compressed spring. Text starts at 30% scale with visible compression (scaleY at 50%), then releases with explosive energy - overshooting to 120% scale before bouncing back through 90% and settling at 100%. Add rapid rotation during launch (0 to 360deg) that decelerates as text settles. This creates high-energy animations perfect for sports content, action sequences, or promotional text that needs serious punch. Imagine editing a sports highlight reel where scores and stats burst onto screen with kinetic force.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Implement with BaseLayout container and TextAtom using complex keyframe array. Scale animation: 0% at {x:0.3, y:0.15}, 40% at {x:1.2, y:1.3}, 60% at {x:0.9, y:0.85}, 100% at {x:1, y:1}. Rotation: 0deg to 360deg with deceleration curve. Use custom spring physics: cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.6, 0.32, 1.6). Total duration 0.7 seconds for impactful but readable result. Add motion blur simulation using multiple shadow copies with decreasing opacity during peak velocity moments. For word-level typography, trigger words sequentially with 0.08 second gaps for machine-gun effect. If caption sentiment data indicates excitement/energy, increase overshoot to 130%. Include 'intensity' parameter to scale all motion values. Apply 'transform-origin: center center' and 'will-change: transform' for optimal rotation.

prompts.prompt: Create a sophisticated 'quantum pop' preset where text materializes through probability clouds - starting as a blurry, jittering ghost at multiple positions before collapsing into final position. Text appears to exist in superposition briefly before 'observing' locks it into place. Begin with 3-5 semi-transparent copies offset by ±10-15px randomly, all at 20% opacity, then converge to center while opacity rises to 100% and scale normalizes. Perfect for sci-fi content, educational physics videos, or anywhere you want to convey uncertainty resolving to clarity. Think of editing a science documentary where quantum concepts need visual representation.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative isolate' for layering. Generate 4 TextAtom instances using repeatChildrenProps with count:4. Each copy starts with random translateX/Y between -15px and 15px, opacity at 0.25, slight blur (1-2px), and scale at 0.9-1.1 (randomized). All copies animate to translateX:0, translateY:0, opacity:1 (except 3 ghost copies fade to 0), blur:0, scale:1 over 0.6 seconds. Use ease-in-out for smooth convergence. Primary copy has z-index:10, ghosts have z-index:1-3. Add subtle shake effect during first 50% of animation using rapid translateX/Y oscillation (±2px at 60fps). For caption implementation, treat each word as its own quantum system with slightly different collapse timing (0.1-0.15 second variance). Include 'quantum-states' parameter to control ghost copy count. Consider using internal effect preset for the convergence animation pattern.
